name: Tiramisù
author: pestanzul on based.cooking
steps: Separate albumen and yolks and beat the latter with the sugar in a bowl.
Add the mascarpone and stir until uniform.
In another bowl, beat the albumens until stiff.
Add beaten albumens to the mascarpone cream gradually, stirring gently to not destroy the foam.
Cover the bottom of a baking tray with a layer of cream.
Cover it with a layer of savoiardi biscuits soaked in coffee.
Add another layer of cream, then another of coffee-soaked savoiardi.
Savoiardi of the second layer should be orthogonal to those of the first, so that the structure is more solid and slices collapse less when they are moved.
Add one last layer of cream.
Store in the fridge for three hours.

culture.text: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert made with coffee-soaked ladyfingers covered with a cream of egg yolks, sugar, mascarpone, and cocoa powder. It originated in northeastern Italy, and modern versions were popularized in restaurants from the late 1960s. Tiramisu has become one of the most internationally recognised Italian desserts and has inspired many variations in home and professional cooking. The name comes from the Italian tirami su, meaning "pick me up" or "cheer me up".
